Rank-one translation maps are enumerated uniquely by their common image line and a 2x2 determinant constraint: each nonzero nilpotent target has q(q^2-1) such pairs and the zero target has (q+1)(q^3+q^2-q-1). All cases follow with q^(4-rank) translation preimages. Exact target multiplicities and weighted total q^12 agree. All-fiber exhaustive direct checks over F2/F3 and independent F4 arithmetic also agree; computations are corroboration, not proof.

The complete five-stratum distribution identifies a geometrically meaningful boundary governed by whether the translation component lies in the image of a rank-one nilpotent matrix.
